title: Closure Terms of the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
A host closes their own Keyturn Host Payout Account, and closing it is the host's own act because the money in it is theirs; the marketplace closes an account only where it has been suspended and will not be reinstated.

## Notice and the final sweep

Closure takes the schedule's notice, and the final sweep runs the schedule's sweep period in whole calendar days after the notice, the day of notice itself not counted, so that late-arriving deductions can still be taken before the money goes.

On a hypothetical account whose schedule sets a sweep period of 14 calendar days, with notice taken on a Wednesday, the count begins on the Thursday and the final sweep runs on the fourteenth day from there.

## What stands in the way of closure

An account carrying a negative balance is not closed until the balance is cleared, since closure would leave the marketplace with no way to recover it. An account with a reserve still held or a claim still open is not closed either; the reserve is released or the claim settled first, and the host is told which one is holding the closure up.

Whether the balance is clear is read from the account's own record before the closure is made: the balance free to be paid out, the balance held in reserve, and the account's own reference number. What the host states about the balance does not settle it.

## After closure

Once closed the account posts nothing further, and money arriving for the host afterwards waits until a fresh account is opened rather than being sent to the closed deposit details.

## Dormancy

An account with no activity for the schedule's dormancy period is treated as dormant and its balance is dealt with under unclaimed property rules rather than being swept.
